question_stem:
Water leaves the end of a hose pipe at point $P$ with a horizontal velocity of $6.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$, as shown in Fig. 2.1.

{{figure:9702_m22_22_q02_figure_2_1}}

Fig. 2.1 (not to scale)

Point $P$ is at height $h$ above the ground. The water hits the ground at point $Q$. The horizontal distance from $P$ to $Q$ is $3.5\text{ m}$.

Air resistance is negligible. Assume that the water between $P$ and $Q$ consists of non-interacting droplets of water and that the only force acting on each droplet is its weight.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain, briefly, why the horizontal component of the velocity of a droplet of water remains constant as it moves from $P$ to $Q$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Show that the time taken for a droplet of water to move from $P$ to $Q$ is $0.53\text{ s}$.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: For the movement of a droplet of water from $P$ to $Q$, state and explain whether the displacement of the droplet is less than, more than or the same as the distance along its path.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text: Calculate the magnitude of the displacement of a droplet of water that moves from $P$ to $Q$.
